feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: it shows clear progression, relevant public-sector depth, and solid technical breadth. The content is polished and specific, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership scope across web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and budget management.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership through a blend of strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve structure and readability.  
- Tighten bullets and add more outcome-focused results. Several bullets describe responsibilities well but could be stronger with measurable business/user outcomes beyond activity and scope.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage could be standardized; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)” instead. Also consider consistent capitalization for “Digital Media Manager / Producer” and date formatting throughout.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas and reducing list-like phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects and skills; “AI-enabled search experiences” is more specific and better supported.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating too many broad capability labels here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experience” for clearer meaning.
- Use “cross-channel” or “omnichannel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid adding tools or examples already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with recent consulting and NACo experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will make it feel more intentional and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise outcome-focused bullet rather than paragraph-style blurbs.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Created AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Clarify scale or purpose where possible: “for policy discovery,” “for campaign growth,” “for conference engagement,” “across web, email, and social.”
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” avoid repeating “built/developed,” and keep punctuation consistent.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite strongly duplicate the current freelance role; consider shortening them or framing them as examples from that engagement.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep only if it adds a distinct cross-channel or program-building angle.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a responsibility list. Tighten it around outcomes, scope, and 3–4 distinctive contributions that complement—not repeat—your NACo leadership bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations for enterprise communications.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance bullets: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits, to speed publishing and improve reuse.”
- Keep the AI/search item, but quantify if possible: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats NACo themes; keep only if you can show a new scale, toolset, or result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may overlap with skills; include only if tied to a notable launch or business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from your earlier NACo positions by focusing on transformation, team leadership, and enterprise systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Led NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine website details into one sharper bullet: “Directed redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen outcomes where possible: add % improvements for traffic, publishing speed, engagement, production cost savings, or reporting adoption from the studio and analytics work.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- “Built NACo’s first…video studio” may echo earlier video-production bullets; frame it here as scaling institutional capacity, not content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial operations and advocacy messaging prior to promotion to Director.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, frequency, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning systems” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- “Weekly video updates” is already referenced in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider adding one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise web governance” or “organization-wide content operations.”
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside broader leadership terms.
- If space allows, use “policy” alongside “public-sector” to better match recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” in Core Competencies; choose one framing.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a curated “topline” skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate Technical + IT section, so this version should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, with the most current/relevant items leading.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Drop “jQuery” here unless it is still central to current work; it feels dated in a topline section.
- If possible, add scope in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., platform size, number of publishers, or search/discovery outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies (“Web & CMS administration”); use one sharper phrase rather than both.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo achievement bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis • GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Put higher-value capabilities first; tools second. “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting” or “decision-support dashboards.”
- Consider tightening to 5–6 items max to improve scanability and seniority.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as “measurement frameworks,” “dashboard development,” or “conversion/engagement analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this section concise to avoid repetition.
- “SEO and performance analysis” partially overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper production language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ/multi-camera studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Studio buildout and operations”
- Lead with the strongest, most distinctive capability: “Broadcast video production” or “Studio buildout and operations” reflects the recent in-house studio achievement better than “video production and editing.”
- Consider dropping “editing” unless it is a differentiator you want to foreground; it can make the line feel more tactical than strategic for a senior digital lead.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect these skills to scale/results in experience bullets rather than listing them here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.
- “Livestreaming” and studio/video work are already evidenced in NACo roles, so avoid expanding this section too much.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a recent senior digital lead profile, this item should either be tighter or add proficiency/context.

Suggested edit
- Keep it concise and recency-weighted: “Drupal (enterprise migration/redesign) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, signal level or use case: “Drupal (advanced), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform experience, with Drupal first and GitHub Pages last.
- If you want more impact, replace the standalone list with: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus modernization work.
- Avoid repeating platform names elsewhere unless this section adds level, scope, or a distinct framing (e.g., CMS only).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/CMS, automation, and web operations work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Web Operations
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier for impact/context: “for CMS customization, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- If GitHub Actions/Cloudflare Workers are not demonstrated in recent roles, consider removing them to avoid overclaiming.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Good tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a tighter, purpose-led label: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools.”
- Prioritize the most relevant systems first and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Teams.”
- Cut weaker/redundant tools if space is tight; keep 5–7 that best support recent work in workflow design and cross-team operations.
- If format allows, add light context instead of only names: “Airtable systems, workflow automation (Power Automate, Zapier), project management (Jira, Asana), team collaboration (Slack, Teams).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each is materially relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or purpose. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and membership communications, frame these as platforms for campaign, newsletter, and audience engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add light context for impact: Used for newsletter operations, member communications, campaign journeys, and audience segmentation
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, order by strongest/recentest use rather than alphabetically

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email references in NACo roles; avoid adding generic phrases like “email newsletters” here unless you specify platform capability
- Don’t duplicate “workflow systems” language already covered under Core Competencies and Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tightening the phrasing and making it more execution-focused will better support the recent NACo and consulting work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboards
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI dashboards” or “executive reporting dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- Consider ordering by strategic depth and recency: analytics stack first, then optimization methods.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in experience bullets instead of adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep one version shorter or differentiate this one as tools only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs rather than team-building language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage buildout and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital communications function across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific deliverables and scale if available: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video series cadence, audience growth, or production volume.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer leadership verb: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later NACo bullets; frame this as early workflow setup, not ongoing operations leadership.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching or initially producing the series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows innovation and multimedia initiative, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim generic support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support member engagement and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member education.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later NACo roles carry the stronger digital leadership story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/digital media entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating workflow/team-building themes already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Creative Software” or “Multimedia Tools” to avoid mixing tools with functions.
- Separate software from production capabilities; keep this line tool-focused.
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want to retain capabilities, move them to the multimedia skills section or rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates “Livestreaming • Studio operations” in Topline Skills.
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older work experience; keep it only if podcasting is still a target-role priority.
